_about: Battle Brothers enemy stats copied exactly from the wiki text in the repo (rule 63d); every row cites its page
_how_read: Source: reference/library/grok/wiki/PAGES_ALL.tar.gz (bb_all/NNNN_Title.txt), the Combatant3 infobox of each unit page, plus the faction unit tables (Brigands, Goblins, Orcs, Zombies, Ancient Dead, Barbarians, Beasts, Noble Houses, City States, Nomads, Mercenaries, Civilian, Humans). A range like '0-45' is copied as the wiki writes it (gear-dependent). conditional_stats = the wiki marks the value with * (it changes with a condition listed in stat_modifiers). unused_stats = the wiki greys the value out (the unit has no use for it). Champion rows carry the wiki's 'With Champion applied' numbers and keep the page's 'Base stats' in stats_before_champion_bonus. champion_chance comes from the faction table. filled_from_table = a value the unit page leaves out but the faction table gives. table_differs = the faction table disagrees with the unit page (page value kept). missing = the field is not given by any source (null). Faction is the side the unit fights for; listed_in = every faction table that lists it.

rows.name: Alp
rows.notes: Alp is a nighttime enemy from the Beasts faction.  Alp groups are only visible and interactable at night. Sometimes there are Direwolves alongside them, including Frenzied ones. Alps fight by first putting their enemies to sleep and then casting nightmares, dealing damage and waking them up. You can wake up an ally for 4 AP, and Rally the Troops wakes up everyone in its range. When one Alp takes damage, they all teleport to tiles one empty space away from you. They have no zone of control, and are unable to break free from nets, and can't even teleport when caught. Fleeing Alps don't actually flee, probably due to a bug. One brother standing near them is enough to prevent rallying, as long as he isn't sleeping.

rows.notes: Armored Unhold is a beast, used for war by Barbarians faction, controlled by Beastmasters.  Unholds usually approach with their Unstoppable Charge, that can't be repelled by a spearwall. They prefer fighting with a regular attack, but can use Fling Back to get close to a vulnerable brother, take the high ground, cancel a shieldwall, or kill someone with 10 HP or less. It's impossible to swap places with Unholds with Barbarian Fury. If not whipped, an Armored Unhold has a 33% chance to turn wild at the start of its turn. Uncontrolled Armored Unholds are hostile to barbarians and controlled Armored Unholds, but not to each other, and they are allied with other Beasts in a three-way fight. Whipped Armored Unholds still retain their wild status until their next turn (verify?). Controlled and wild Armored Unholds can be distinguished by their tokens' bases. Barbarians' base means it's controlled, and Beasts' base indicates it's wild.

- If he is a Necromancer's bodyguard, 50% chance for a Decayed Heater Shield or Old Wooden Shield.

rows.notes: Armored Wiederganger is an enemy from the Zombies faction.  Wiedergangers come in large numbers. They have know any idea about careful approach and instead slowly walk towards you, getting hit by spearwalls. They have a 66% chance to raise from the dead on their own once with 50% HP. When they do so, it causes a morale check similar to coming into melee. They can reanimate if someone stands on their corpse, and will push that unit one tile away. If there is nowhere to push, they stay dead. They can not revive if their head has been decapitated or smashed, but can if disemboweled. If they kill a human, he can rise as a Wiederganger too. He uses stats of Wiederganger Brother and "Wiederganger" is added before his name. Sometimes they lose their weapons when they die. They can pick up weapons from the ground if this happens. They are unable to use ranged weapons, and they can only use basic and area weapon attacks. They don't spawn with weapons with area attacks though. Bodyguards can knock you with their shields to push away from Necromancers.

They will use Adrenaline to get ahead of the enemy if not already faster than them. They will use Footwork to get close to someone vulnerable and attack him. They can throw Fire Pots and Flash Pots, but no more than two in total per Assassin. They don't actually have bombs in the inventory, but create them when they want to throw. If you manage to defeat an Assassin with a bomb in hand, it will even drop as loot!

rows.notes: Barbarian King is a dangerous, heavily armored elite enemy from the Barbarians faction, encountered in a contract to hunt him.  Barbarian Kings only appear in contracts to hunt them. Their warbands are visible from twice the usual distance. Only one King will be in it. If attacked by a stronger non-player squad on the world map, the King always survives by the virtue of having plot armor, defeating the enemy army alone. The contract of course becomes much easier in this case. Like all barbarians, he moves forward and attacks the enemy. He will use Adrenaline to get ahead of the enemy if not already faster than them. Usually he waits after acting, and activates it at the very end. He can rotate with other barbarians to save a wounded ally, attack someone vulnerable, or without a clear purpose. If he escapes, the contract does not fail and continues as if you have killed him, including bringing his head to the nobleman.

rows.notes: Fallen Betrayer is a heavily armored elite enemy from the Zombies faction, found in the Watermill legendary location.  They are based on the Fallen Hero's template, but have better stats, similarly to Lost Treasure Hunters. They don't know any idea about careful approach and instead simply walk towards you, getting hit by spearwalls. They have a 90% chance to raise from the dead on their own once with 50% HP. When they do it, it causes a morale check similar to coming into melee. They can reanimate if someone stands on their corpse, and will push that unit one tile away. If there is nowhere to push, they stay dead. They can rise headless, and if they do, all head hits they take are redirected to the body. They still can bite even with no head. If they kill a human, he can rise as a Wiederganger. He uses stats of Wiederganger Brother and a "Wiederganger" is added before his name. Sometimes they lose their weapons when they die. They can pick up weapons from the ground if this happens. They are unable to use ranged weapons, and they can only use basic and area weapon attacks.

rows.notes: Goblin Wolfrider is a fast enemy from the Goblins faction.  Wolfriders are fast enemies that avoid direct combat if they see backliners unguarded from the rear. They will circle around you, trying to get to them. However, when everyone is guarded properly, Wolfriders simply charge like regular enemies. They will use Footwork to get close to someone vulnerable and attack him. When they die, either a Skirmisher or a Wolf spawns, depending on where the last hit landed. Head hit spawns a Wolf, which then acts immediately, and body hit spawns a normal variant of Skirmisher. The enemy will always have 45% of its HP and the same morale as the Wolfrider, however fleeing is replaced with breaking. Skirmishers also retain the armor. rows.name: Hexe
rows.notes: Hexe is a spellcaster from the Beasts faction, guarded by beasts or brigands, charmed by her.  Hexen have no zone of control, and are unable to break free from nets. They can cast both Charm and Hex on the same turn if not capped on fatigue. When using Charm, Hexen prefer brothers with low resolve, dangerous weapons, many adjacent brothers to create a zone of control over them, unguarded ranged brothers, or those who threaten them or are in melee already. Hexen are less likely to target brothers with high resolve, weak weapons, guarded ranged brothers and those who waits with low AP. Charm is prioritized over Hex and will be used when capped on fatigue. When using Hex, Hexen prefer wounded targets, especially having an effect like Bleeding that will kill them, and prefer brothers over allies in three-way fights. They avoid using Hex against brothers with Indomitable, even inactive, or low level poorly armored brothers. Taunt causes them to Hex the taunting brother. They only cast Hex when they think they are in danger, and even then not always do it. Their allies get +20 resolve from the fake charmed status. Some of them guard Hexen, staying near them. Fleeing Hexen don't actually flee, probably due to a bug. One brother standing near them is enough to prevent rallying, as long as he isn't charmed. They seem to have 8 vision instead of 7 that units have normally.

Unlike Direwolves, sometimes they can wait. They can not have these injuries: Fractured Hand Crushed Finger Fractured Elbow Smashed Hand Broken Arm Cut Arm Sinew Cut Arm Split Hand Pierced Hand Pierced Arm Muscles Burnt Hands

rows.name: Ifrit (Small)
stat_modifiers: +5 initiative if there is a same sized Ifrit adjacent, +10 if two or more
rows.notes: Ifrit is a creature of sand and stone from the Beasts faction. They come in three sizes, larger being formed when smaller merge together.  Ifrits can merge together and break apart. When they do it, all damage they had is repaired. Larger ones are tougher and hit harder. Three adjacent Ifrits of the same size can combine into a larger Ifrit, except when they are large already. They prioritize assembling above anything else. Medium and large Ifrits can throw a part of themselves, breaking apart in the process. Medium Ifrits break into three small ones, one of which is thrown. Large Ifrits break into two medium and three small ones, one of which is thrown. They can't throw if there is not enough space for all parts, medium Ifrits need one tile near them and large need three. If killed, they also break apart, but without one small part, and more parts are lost if there are no free adjacent tiles for them. They all have no heads, all head hits are redirected to the body. Medium and large Ifrits have a unique mechanic that affects armor. They have ArmorMult values modified, set to 2 and 4 respectively. It multiplies the armor value, but only in HP damage calculations. Armor damage is not affected. Mods that show exact armor value usually show it multiplied.

rows.name: Kraken
rows.notes: Kraken is the boss of the Stone Pillars legendary location. Its tentacles are called Irrlichts.  Kraken fight has two phases. In the first phase tentacles always try to grab brothers and drag them to the head, which has a guaranteed instant kill attack hitting all tiles adjacent to it. Entangled brothers are dragged at the start of their turn. Tentacles respawn when killed, and Kraken takes HP damage, 190 initially, but decreases by 5 with each tentacle to a minimum of 35. The second phase begins when its HP drops below half, or when six tentacles die. Tentacles gain a high damage bite attack, but sometimes will still entangle, and they begin to deal 10-15 HP damage to entangled characters. In this phase, as the Kraken's HP lowers, so does the number of tentacles. Kraken loses one tentacle at each of 43,75%, 37,5%, 31,25% and 25% HP thresholds. Breaking free from tentacles is similar to nets. Successfully disentangling damages the tentacle for 15-30 damage, but leaves it with at least 25 HP. Kraken head and its tentacles are not affected by morale and have no zone of control. Body hits that Kraken head takes are redirected to the head. Krakens generate with the following names, however the first one is always named Beast of Beasts. stat_modifiers: Melee skill is 75 before day 170, 85 after
rows.notes: Lindwurm is a dangerous two-tile enemy from the Beasts faction. It has separate head and tail tokens.  Lindwurm is a two-tile monster. Its head and tail occupy separate tiles. They share HP, armor, fatigue and morale. When the head acts, the tail acts right after it. The tail tries to stay close to the head, but sometimes becomes disconnected. The tail ignores zone of control. Fatigue decreases only on head's turns. Effects like Bleeding, Daze, Taunt and Overwhelm affect each part separately. Injuries are not shared and only affect the head. Non-critical hits to the head are redirected to the body. Critical hits to the tail are not redirected but do critical damage and inflict head injuries. If the tail is hit by Split Man, all damage goes to the body. Both head and body will splash attackers with acid when hit for 10 damage, but only if attacked from adjacent tiles. Being next to one part and attacking the other of the same Lindwurm from a safe distance will still splash with acid.

rows.notes: Lost Treasure Hunter is an enemy found in the Sunken Library legendary location.  They are based on the Fallen Hero's template, but have better stats, similarly to Fallen Betrayers, and different equipment. They don't know any idea about careful approach and instead simply walk towards you, getting hit by spearwalls. They have a 90% chance to raise from the dead on their own once with 50% HP. When they do it, it causes a morale check similar to coming into melee. They can reanimate if someone stands on their corpse, and will push that unit one tile away. If there is nowhere to push, they stay dead. They can rise headless, and if they do, all head hits they take are redirected to the body. They still can bite even with no head. If they kill a human, he can rise as a Wiederganger. He uses stats of Wiederganger Brother and a "Wiederganger" is added before his name. Sometimes they lose their weapons when they die. They can pick up weapons from the ground if this happens. They are unable to use ranged weapons, and they can only use basic and area weapon attacks.

rows.notes: Mortar is a southern war machine, operated by Engineers.  Mortars only fire if loaded by an Engineer. rows.name: Nachzehrer (Small)
rows.notes: Nachzehrer is a ghoul-like enemy from the Beasts faction. They come in three sizes.  Nachzehrers come in three sizes. Larger ones have more HP, damage, resolve, melee skill and defense, but less ranged defense. It's not uncommon to see one large Nachzehrer among small ones in the early game. They have the ability to eat corpses, including those of their own kind, to grow in size, fully heal and improve morale. They are attracted to corpses and will try reaching them even if there is a spearwall or sometimes even if they are already in a zone of control. The largest variant does not grow, but still can heal itself by eating corpses. It also can swallow a character alive. That character takes a bit of non-lethal damage and his morale is set to Breaking. There is no damage over time. When the Nachzehrer is slain, the character returns to battle. However he will die if you let the Nachzehrer escape with him. This ability is only used against player units. Nachzehrers approach somewhat carefully and often wait for an opportunity to occupy a tile with a corpse and eat it on the next turn. They take damage from Flasks of Blessed Water.

rows.notes: Necromancer is a spellcaster from the Zombies faction. He isn't undead himself.  Necromancers stay far behind their undead minions and cast spells from there. There is rarely more than one of them. They are guarded by two undead bodyguards who have shields and will try to Knock Back anyone who gets near a Necromancer. On the first turn, however, they sometimes can become exposed to shots. They cast Possess Undead to make an undead more dangerous, prioritizing those who are in melee already, and Fallen Heroes over Wiedergangers if they have a choice. They can cast it twice per turn, waiting after the first cast. Also they cast Raise Undead to bring an undead back to unlife with full HP. They again prefer to cast it on Fallen Heroes. If the tile with the corpse if occupied, they are unable to raise it. They also can raise corpses of normal humans killed in battle, which use stats of Wiederganger Brother and a "Wiederganger" is added before their names. They can't cast spells if engaged in melee. rows.notes: Necrosavant is a dangerous enemy from the Ancient Dead faction.  Necrosavants are extremely mobile and do not respect zones of control, because they can teleport. They don't like to be surrounded and will teleport away even if adjacent to two brothers. But Taunt has such great effect on them so they even teleport into surrounding in response. Interestingly, they have no unarmed attack.

They prefer to drag more vulnerable units, units that are not engaded in melee, and especially they like to drag someone with Shieldwall, Spearwall or Riposte active, canceling these skills. They are also more likely to drag if they aren't in melee themselves. Taunt has little effect and only affects their melee attack. They can not have these injuries: Fractured Hand Crushed Finger Fractured Elbow Sprained Ankle Bruised Leg Smashed Hand Broken Arm Broken Leg Cut Arm Sinew Cut Arm Cut Achilles Tendon Split Hand Injured Shoulder Pierced Hand Pierced Arm Muscles Injured Knee Cap Burnt Leg Burnt Hands

gear_detail: - A Crypt Cleaver.
- A weaker version of The Emperor's Armor (380).
- An Ancient Laurels (50).
rows.notes: Conqueror is the boss of the Black Monolith legendary location.  His body armor is notable for its ability to reflect 25% of received damage back to the attacker. That damage always hits body and does not pierce armor. While the tooltip says that it reflects melee damage, it's not always true. Damage is actually reflected if the attacker is adjacent, and the attack does not have to be melee. So being two tiles away and attacking with a polearm does not trigger reflection, but point blank crossbow shot does. Reflection continues to work even after the armor is destroyed. His armor does not drop. The Emperor's Armor you get after the battle is a different item.

rows.name: The Grand Diviner
gear_detail: - The Censer of the Diviner.
- Robes of Divination (125).
- A Cowl of Divination (75).
rows.notes: The Grand Diviner is the boss of the Artifact Reliquary legendary location.  Grand Diviner will use Adrenaline to strike first. He has Footwork and can use it offensively to reach and strike someone vulnerable. When he dies and any Fault Finders are present, one of them is chosen to resurrect the Diviner. The Fault Finder dies and the Diviner respawns on his tile, has his equipment repaired and morale set to confident, and a miasma cloud is created on the tile where he was originally killed. If no Fault Finders remain and you kill him, none of this happens and he does not respawn. His flail does not drop, you get it in the event after the battle. Armor and helmet drop normally, no matter how damaged they were or how many times you killed the Grand Diviner.

rows.name: The Ijirok
rows.notes: Ijirok is the boss of the Hunting Ground legendary location.  Every turn Ijirok will teleport away, freezing the space around it, and then ram into your squad from different directions. On the first turn it just rams. It is not affected by morale and has no zone of control.

rows.name: The Lorekeeper
gear_detail: - The Black Book.
- An Ancient Attire (60).
- An Ancient Headpiece (80).
rows.notes: Lorekeeper is the boss of the Sunken Library legendary location.  Lorekeeper has a very complex behavior. The most important things are that he can't die if any Phylacteries remain intact and will respawn from them, and the fight gets harder when you destroy more Phylacteries. Some Ancient Honor Guards will guard him, not actively attacking you and making the battle easier. His Miasma and Horror have to range limit. He has no zone of control. He can traverse steep cliffs (verify). ===Variables=== Let f be the number of remaining Phylacteries. Let r be the round number. ===Skills availability=== Lorekeeper's skill set is defined by f - {r \over 7}: ===Summoning skulls=== Lorekeeper can summon Screaming Skulls once per turn. Skulls spawn 5-6 tiles away from your brothers. To simplify, he summons 4-12 skulls per turn to a limit of 12-30 on the map, depending on how many Phylacteries were destroyed. Exact mechanics: Let x = \max(0, 9 - \max(0, f - {r \over 9})) . Summoned per turn: \min(x + 4, 12). Limit: 2x + 12. ===Summoning apparitions=== In the middle of battle Lorekeeper starts summoning Apparitions, ghostly copies of himself. They spawn far away from you and will cast spells too. To simplify, there will be four of them as it's not worth spending time hunting them. Exact mechanics: Summoned per turn: \max(0, 6 - \max(0, f - {r \over 9})) + 2 . Limit is 4. === Lightnings === Lorekeeper can mark a vertical line on the ground to strike it with lightnings on the next turn. Apparitions also do it, but with one turn of cooldown after the actual strike. [...]

rows.name: Unhold
rows.notes: Unhold is an enemy from the Beasts faction. There are three slightly different species of them.  Unholds usually approach with their Unstoppable Charge, that can't be repelled by a spearwall. They prefer fighting with a regular attack, but can use Fling Back to get close to a vulnerable brother, take the high ground, cancel a shieldwall, or kill someone with 10 HP or less. Scripts contain code that spawns Bog Unholds in oasises, and their behavior only allows them to roam swamps and leafy forests, not oasises.

rows.name: Webknecht
stat_modifiers: Melee defense is 10 before day 50, 15 after
Ranged defense is 20 before day 50, 25 after
+5% direct damage dealt at day 25-50, +10% after
2x direct damage dealt to Webbed targets
rows.notes: Webknecht is a giant spider, a weak enemy from the Beasts faction.  Webknechts are very numerous, and will also generate Webknecht Eggs that spawn even more. The number of eggs is 5 times less than spiders, and each egg can spawn 4 of them. Spiders that hatched don't drop loot and their XP reward is halved. Eggs only appear when there is more than 5 spiders. Webknechts can traverse steep cliffs. Webknechts are beasts dumb enough to run into spearwall or come close without being able to attack. They sometimes run into surrounding and footwork away. They almost always prioritize web over bite. They can't have these injuries: Fractured Hand Crushed Finger Fractured Elbow Smashed Hand Broken Arm Cut Arm Sinew Cut Arm Split Hand Pierced Hand Pierced Arm Muscles Burnt Hands

rows.name: Webknecht Eggs
rows.notes: Webknecht Eggs appear in fights with Webknechts and spawn more of them.  The number of eggs is 5 times less than spiders, but a group of 5 spiders don't spawn eggs. They are placed on tiles where they are not seen by the player, and are never hidden in vegetation. Eggs are stationary and aren't in turn order. However, they can spawn a Webknecht at round start. Webknechts hatch with a delay of 1 or 2 turns randomly, can't act on the round they hatched, drop no loot and their XP reward is halved. After spawning 4 spiders Eggs self-destruct. They all instantly die if there are no more spiders on the map.

rows.name: Wiederganger
gear_detail: - 50% chance of a Bludgeon, Militia Spear, Butcher's Cleaver, Pickaxe, Wooden Stick, Knife or Pitchfork.
- A Leather Tunic (30), Apron (25), Butcher's Apron (25), Linen Tunic (20) (double chance), Monk's Robe (20), Leather Wraps (20), Sackcloth (10) or Tattered Sackcloth (5).
- 33% chance of a Full Aketon Cap (50), Full Leather Cap (45), Aketon Cap (40), Open Leather Cap (40) or Hood (30).

rows.notes: Wiederganger is a weak enemy from the Zombies faction.  Wiedergangers come in large numbers. They don't have any idea about careful approach and instead slowly walk towards you, getting hit by spearwalls. They have a 66% chance to raise from the dead on their own once with 50% HP. When they do so, it causes a morale check similar to coming into melee. They can reanimate if someone stands on their corpse, and will push that unit one tile away. If there is nowhere to push, they stay dead. They can not revive if their head has been decapitated or smashed, but can if disemboweled. If they kill a human, he can rise as a Wiederganger too. He uses stats of Wiederganger Brother and "Wiederganger" is added before his name. They can pick up weapons from the ground. They are unable to use ranged weapons, and they can only use basic and area weapon attacks. They don't spawn with weapons with area attacks though.

He isn't literally named brother but a "Wiederganger" is added before his name. They are unable to use ranged weapons, and they can only use basic and area weapon attacks.

When they do so, it causes a morale check similar to coming into melee. They can reanimate if someone stands on their corpse, and will push that unit one tile away. They are unable to use ranged weapons, and they can only use basic and area weapon attacks. Bodyguards can knock you with their shields to push away from Necromancers.
